newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec S&P 500 futures finish slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec S&P 500 futures finish slightly lower.

text.p: U.S. December Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished slightly lower in moderate trading, under seige from profit-taking.

December S&Ps moved to a fresh contract and record high at 736.25 in Globex trading and tried again early, but fell just short of the high at 736.20. Longs then turned aggressive sellers to take the market into negative territory, traders said. They said fund selling played a key role in the sell-off.
Traders noted stops hit below 732.30 in December, but said the market absorbed the selling well.
"A little bit of selling is not unhealthy for this market," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
After such strong gains last week, stock index futures were due to set back, traders said. Dec S&Ps rallied more than 30.0 points from last Monday's low at 705.95 to the record high today at 736.25.
December Nasdaq futures also surged to a fresh high early then collapsed, below psychologically key 800.00. Traders tied the Nasdaq decline to a plunge in Intel after hitting a year-high.
"It's kind of a shake-out," the S&P trader said.
"It's a tug of war with the strong bonds and the weak Nasdaq," he said.

Traders said the market was a bit jittery heading into key U.S. inflation data Wednesday and Thursday. The Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Wednesday was expected to yield no change in monetary policy and was largely considered a non-event, traders said.
Wednesday's producer price index is seen rising 0.2 percent overall and 0.1 percent in the core rate.
Thursday's October consumer price index is forecast up 0.3 percent overall and 0.2 percent ex-food and energy.
October retail sales, due on Thursday, are forecast up 0.3 percent overall and in the core rate.
U.S. data on Tuesday had little impact on the market, traders said.

Richmond Federal Reserve Bank's manufacturing new orders index rose in October to 2 from minus 4 in September. U.S. adjusted retail sales rose 0.5 percent in the first week in November versus October, Redbook Research reported.

Dec S&P 500 futures finished down 2.10 points to 732.00, Dec Nikkei 225 futures ended up 170.0 points to 21270.0, CME's Russell 2000 index lost 1.20 points to 347.00, New York composities lose 0.85 point to 387.25, Kansas City Value Lines gained 0.60 point to 663.70 and Nasdaq 100 futures lost 11.10 to 798.40.
